integrity: The classification is a bijection. Divisibility by the digit product first forces the trailing digit to be a multiple of the leading digit; normalizing that multiple converts the condition exactly into a divisor d of the base and a proper divisor of d+1. The count and extremal equality criterion follow without computational assumptions; finite enumeration is corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem classifies only exactly two-digit base-b Zuckerman numbers. The inspected literature contains general asymptotic and algorithmic counting results, but no explicit two-digit divisor-lattice formula was located. An equivalent elementary observation may exist in unindexed recreational literature. Older bibliographic appearances lack an exact public calendar day in the inspected evidence, so the stored date uses the earliest exact public day verified here.
title: Divisor-lattice formula for two-digit Zuckerman numbers
